main_text.l: Iulius Obsequiens prodigium triste Vibio Pansę factum scribit, quod equus faleratus in ipsius conspectu festinans concidit. Denique hunc talem inter imperij insignia Dionysius ponit, de L. Quinctio Dictatore ad aratrum capto: Ἵππους τε αὐτῷ φαλάρεις κεκοσμημένους εὐπρεπέσι θεσσήγον[?], καὶ πελέκεις ἅμα ταῖς ῥάβδοις, ἐδη̂ταῖς τε ἀλλεργάς[?], καὶ τὰ ἄλλα ἄσυμα[?] τῆς ἀρχῆς: Equos ipsi phaleris decoris ornatos admouerunt,& secures cum fascibus,vestesque purpuratas;& alia imperij insignia. Ac vidi in columnâ illâ Traiani, cum in Italiâ essem, hos tales exstare sculptos, & haud longè Principem à Stratoribus duci. An non apud Graecos simile? De Alexandro quidem Cur-tius scripsit, Taxili inter alia dona misisse triginta equos ex suis, cum iisdem insignibus, quis assueuerant cum ipsum veherent.

page.notes: The left strip is the edge of the neighbouring page and was left out. The Greek words marked [?] are uncertain on the scan. The reading of the Greek line break "θεσσήγον" and "ἐδη̂ταῖς" and "ἀλλεργάς" and "ἄσυμα" is doubtful. The name "Pansę" with the cedilla-like ę is uncertain. The "&" signs are printed as a ligature-like ampersand. The first paragraph starts without an indent and is taken as a continuation from the previous page.
